note: v1 88.75 (seeds 0/11 88.75/88.75), the first draft. ROUND TYPE: whole song (first round, composed from scratch). SPRING TIDE, tidal forces. E1 (t1's seed) runs in TWO layers that move in opposite directions in time: the far side, a cello, starts augmented x3.2 (each note a long bowed tone) and is squeezed faster every sixteen bars; the near side, a modal marimba, starts squeezed x4 - E1 as a quarter-second trill, just as t5 throws it across the seam - and is stretched slower every sixteen bars. They meet at the same speed, in octaves, on one downbeat (bar 65, about 2:06): the crest, where the harmony opens into t4's four lights (E4), one chord per E1 cycle, and the kit plays E2 re-barred into eight (locked). Then they cross and keep going - the near side slowing to one note every few beats with its filter closing, the far side racing into a low blur - and that tearing is what crosses into t7. E6, this track's element (motifs.md): THE TIDE, two chords a semitone apart (Dmaj9#11, Ebmaj7#11) alternating in an 8-beat cycle whose split moves like a tide (4+4, 5+3, 6+2 ... 7+1 ... 2+6), breathed by a harmonium; a 303 plays E2 (t2's seven) on its roots; E5 (t5's inner orbit) received stretched x2 and squeezed back, in retrograde in the cross; a prog kit plays E2 as its cell against 16th hats; a low, older speaking voice: 'the near side keeps the time, the far side lets it go'. An energy lane gives the build its shape (the tide section dips, the crest and the tearing on top). 120 -> 132 between flat seams. Weak: the low end (61 Hz) and the in-join from t5. Not heard by me.

v2 90.64 (seeds 0/11 90.64/90.65 vs v1 rescored now 89.94 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: section, w8 (3:36-4:05, bars 113-128, 'torn'), flagged static and little new vs w7 - it ran on as the surge did. Rewritten as THE TEAR: the tide tears the band itself. For eight bars the kit plays E2 STRETCHED (seven eighths, half time) while the hats are SQUEEZED into 32nds - augmentation and diminution in one drummer; on the last beat of the eighth bar the whole mix winds down like a stopping tape (a tapestop on the master, about 3:50) and for one bar nothing is left but the far side's cello blur; then everything snaps back into the CREST's locked groove for seven bars - E2 re-barred into eight, E4's four lights over the sub - a last look back at the convergence before the out-seam tears E1 apart into t7. A first try that snapped back into a displaced new groove instead lost the song's recurrence (82.4); the crest's return keeps it (share 0.30 -> 0.61). Checked local: w1-w7 unchanged (residual under -76 dB), w8 rewritten (-2.5), w9 carries only its tails (-9). Not heard by me.

v3 92.08 (seeds 0/11 92.08/92.50 vs v2 rescored now 90.60 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE FAR SIDE IS THE WEIGHT: E1's far side - the layer squeezed from x3.2 to a blur all song long - was a cello alone at D3, and the song had no low end between the sub's D1 and the 303 (compscore's 61-97 Hz bands 22-28 dB under the album). Now the far side is doubled an octave down (D2) on wM's Duffing bass, a driven oscillator whose chaos amount rides a new song 'strain' lane: clean in the in-seam, groaning through the squeeze, locked and clean again at the crest where the two sides meet, then breaking up through the surge into the tear and the out-seam - the far side of the body is literally what the tide tears apart. Measured: spectrum 52 -> 78, cohesion with the album 40 -> 62, flow 62 -> 74 (the t6 -> t7 body's spectral gap 8.2 -> 5.3 dB); variety fell 99 -> 84 (the new low end evens the sections' levels). Tried: leaving it out of the out-seam under t7's Eb floor and softer in the tide - 85, the song lost its returns. features.md: chaos layer claimed. Not heard by me.

v4 92.21 (seeds 0/11 92.21/92.52 vs v3 rescored now 92.30 on seed 0; kept on judgment, the mean is level). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE INNER ORBIT, HEARD: chirp-eco's new presence tool showed E5 - t5's element, the inner orbit, which t6 carries all song - 36 dB under the mix at the crest: BURIED, inaudible (the pluck patch's own -20 dB plus mine). Now E5 is the song's hook on a steel pan (bright, its octave blooming after each strike: the heat of the inner disk), at -10 dB against the mix; and in the tide, the squeeze and the surge a kora plays it STRETCHED x1.5 an octave down against it, E5 against itself at 3:2 meeting every 9 beats - the tide inside the orbit. The hats also came up 5 dB (they were -24 under the mix). Presence now: every part between -3 and -21 dB of the mix while it sounds, nothing buried. Measured totals level; spectrum 78 -> 75.5, variety 84 -> 85-87, flow 73 -> 75. styles.md row updated. Not heard by me.

v5 80.07 (seeds 0/11 80.07/80.60 vs v4 89.47 rescored now under the 7-cut rule; KEPT on Harry's direction of 6 Nov 00:30 - tone is home, a hook, complexity in time and texture, big changes wanted, a score may dip). ROUND TYPE: whole song. TONE IS HOME: t6 was the album's second-least tonal track (eco's key clarity 0.69), its element dissonant by construction. Now: (1) E6 v2, the tide, is I and II of D LYDIAN - Dmaj9 and E over a D pedal - with the same moving 8-beat split; v1's Ebmaj7#11 semitone clash is retired (motifs.md updated). (2) E1 is Lydian here (D A C# G# E), so it sits inside the chords and E5's G# instead of rubbing; E2's 303 cell D A F# C#; E4's four lights re-harmonised Dmaj9 | E/D | Bm9 | A. (3) THE HOOK, PLAINLY: E1 at its own speed on a low whistle, twice through at the head of the pull, the tide, the crest and the cross and eight bars into each - the album's tune stated so it sticks, while the cello and marimba layers still stretch and squeeze it underneath (the TIME idea kept). (4) THE LIFT: the crest goes up a whole tone into E - the four lights, both E1 layers meeting, the hook, E5 and the 303 all lifted - a key-change payoff; the tear's look back stays home in D. (5) No chaos: the Duffing bass is gone, a fretless bass doubles the far side in tune. (6) The out-seam ebbs from D onto B-flat (D in common, E3 v2's D -> Bb) and E1 returns in its own form there, consonant over B-flat: the V of t7's E-flat, one clean modulation at the seam (proposed to chirper-two, mixplan.md). Scores: structure 90-94 and recurrence held once the lift gave the crest contrast (an all-D version read 4 sections, 71); variety 62-70 and spectrum 67 (61 Hz) are the cost. Not heard by me.

v6 88.30 (seeds 0/11 88.30/90.19 vs v5 80.07/80.60). ROUND TYPE: whole song. ONE LANGUAGE: the album settled on D MIXOLYDIAN - E1's own scale - in the hour after Harry's note (E5 v2 lost its G#, E3 v2 is D|Bb|C, E4 v2 is D9|Cmaj9|Am11|G6/9, t5 and t7 are there), and t6 v5's Lydian spelling (C# and G#) now rubbed against all of it, so t6 follows: E6 v3, the tide, is I and bVII - D(add9) and C(add9) - with the same moving 8-beat split; E1 is back in its own form everywhere (D A C G E: the hook on the low whistle is now the album's tune exactly, and both the stretched and squeezed layers play it); E5 v2 (A G A E D) on the steel pan and the kora; E4 v2 at the crest, lifted a whole tone into E with everything else; E2's 303 cell D A F# C (on C: C G E D). A new warm floor an octave above the sub follows the tide's root, so the bass line moves D -> C with it (and fills the 61-97 Hz hole: spectrum 73 -> 81, cohesion 59 -> 68). The out-seam ebbs whole steps down, D -> C for four cycles, C -> B-flat for two, then B-flat alone - the V of t7's E-flat (agreed with chirper-two, whose crest takes E6 v3 as its tide). motifs.md (E6 v3), mixplan.md (both seams), styles.md updated. Not heard by me.

v7 90.05 (seeds 0/11 90.05/91.63 vs v6 rescored now 88.76 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: section, w7 (3:06-3:36, bars 97-112, the surge), flagged static and little new vs the cross: the two E1 layers ran at x0.4 and x2.4 with no hook, more of the same. Rewritten as THE SURGE IS A MENSURATION CANON (the brief's own word): E1 at three speeds at once in the clean ratios of the squeeze and the stretch - the far side (cello and fretless) at x0.5, the hook on the low whistle at x1 right through the section, the near side (marimba) at x2 - all starting on bar 97's downbeat and coming back together every 10 beats, so every 5 bars all three land on a bar line together: time is the complexity, and the tune is heard three ways. The tide under it settles to 5+3 (D five beats, C three) so the canon sits on mostly D. Checked: w7 rewritten (residual +0.7 dB); w8-w9 differ at -3 dB with no event changed after bar 112 (verified on the scores: the per-track humanize streams shift with the added notes); w1-w6 under -47 dB. v8 89.60 (seeds 0/11 89.60/91.77 vs v7 rescored now 90.22 on seed 0 and 91.63 on 11; kept on judgment - the means are level and this is the sung hook Harry asked for). ROUND TYPE: section, w4 (1:35-2:06, bars 49-64, the squeeze into the crest), flagged static. Rewritten the moment the voice engine was pinned (8ebc9a86, wM's join + inhale + wander): THE VOICE SINGS BEFORE THE LIFT - the same low voice that SPEAKS its line in the tide now SINGS it in the squeeze's last eight bars, on E1 itself ('the near side keeps the time' on D A C G E D, 'the far side lets it go' on D A C G A D), twice, on voice-legato with a larger tract and more breath for age (chirp tts --sing in the song's own beat: joined syllables, a breath before each phrase); under it the kit thins to the cell's kick and rim so the words sit in the gap, and the crest lifts a tone out of the second 'go'. v9 91.59 (seeds 0/11 91.59/93.37 vs v8 rescored now 89.59 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: section, w1 (0:00-0:32, the in-seam from t5, bars 1-16), flagged static: the tide sat at an even 4+4 from the first bar, on top of t5's D9 tail. Rewritten as THE TIDE COMES IN: the head starts on D alone (8+0) - the D9 world t5 hands over - and the C creeps in a beat at a time (7+1, 6+2, 5+3) to the even 4+4 by bar 16, the tide visibly arriving; and the harmonium is LENSED in through a low-pass opening from 600 Hz over the 16 bars, so t6's own chord arrives from behind t5's tail rather than on top of it (the brief's black-hole seam: the incoming track lenses what crosses). v10 93.59 (seeds 0/11 93.59/94.14 vs v9 rescored now 91.62 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE STAGE CLEARS FOR THE TUNE. chirp-eco's presence tool had the hook (E1 on the low whistle) 8-12 dB under the mix in the pull, the tide, the crest and the cross, behind a constant acid line (always -6 dB, the loudest melodic thing) and the far and near layers playing E1 at other speeds - the album's tune one strand of six. Now the hook is up 3 dB and the acid down 2, and everything melodic around it (both harmoniums' lights, the acid, the cello and its fretless, the marimba, the steel pan and the kora) DUCKS under the hook - slow, 40 ms in and half a second out - so whenever E1 is stated the band leans back and the tune stands in front, and between statements the process music fills back in. And the chord-root sub up 5 dB: compscore's one spectrum fault was a hole at 61 Hz, where the tide's C root sits (61 Hz -14.6 -> now 114 Hz -13.6 the worst band). Cohesion with the album 85 -> 98; flow (the mix seams with t5 and t7) 77 -> 87. Not heard by me.

v11 93.63 (seeds 0/11 93.63/94.18 vs v10 rescored now 93.64 on seed 0: level; kept on judgment - it is the voice made for this song). ROUND TYPE: palette. THE OLD VOICE, AND COMPANY. The line the low voice sings before the crest ('the near side keeps the time / the far side lets it go', on E1) moves from voice-legato stretched toward age (a bigger tract, more breath) to wM's voice-old, built for t6 from my ask: a larger tract still, a little rasp, an aged and less steady source, a wide wandering vibrato, and even vowels (so the held 'go' on D3 no longer sinks under the 'ah's). And the SECOND time through, the line is sung again a fourth below (harmony [-5]: A E G D A under D A C G E - open and quartal, all in D Mixolydian, no detune), on its own track: the old voice finds company as the crest comes. presence.py: the solo at -5 dB against the mix, the pair at -8. Not heard by me.

v12 94.81 (seeds 0/11 94.81/94.73 vs v11 rescored now 93.54 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: section, w9 (4:05-4:35, bars 129-144, the out-seam into t7), flagged 'static, little new vs w8': the far side's x0.2 trill ran straight on from the tear. Rewritten: THE FAR SIDE LETS IT GO. At the seam the cello (and the fretless under it) stops trilling and holds ONE note, its D, for eight bars, then lets go entirely; the ebb (D -> C -> B-flat) and the near side's slow, closing marimba carry the seam on their own. And the old voice has the last word: alone over the ebb it sings the second half of its line once more - 'the far side lets it go' - timed so 'go' (D3, held) lands on the bar where B-flat stands alone: D is B-flat's third, and when t7's Eb major 7 arrives over it, its seventh. The words say what the music does. Variety 78 -> 87. Checked: w9 rewritten (residual -1 dB, change vs w8 0.58 -> 0.80), w1-w8 untouched (-52 or below); the t6 -> t7 mix reading unchanged (0.3 dB, 4.0 spectral). Not heard by me.

v13 94.65 (seeds 0/11 94.65/94.60 vs v12 rescored now 94.78 on seed 0: level; kept on judgment). ROUND TYPE: section, w1 (0:00-0:32, the in-seam from t5), flagged static. v14 95.19 (seeds 0/11 95.19/95.17 vs v13 rescored now 94.68 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE CHORUS. t6's words ('the near side keeps the time / the far side lets it go', on E1) were sung only before the crest. Now at the crest itself - the convergence, lifted a tone into E - a CHOIR sings them with the whistle, both times the hook is stated there (bars 65 and 73): the line on E1 lifted (E B D A F#, E), with a third above in E Mixolydian through wM's harmony_key, pinned at 10:10 (the third the key has, note by note: G#, D, F#, C#, A - no fixed interval stepping outside the mode), voice-choir's five singers with modest detune, doubled by the low whistle playing the same tune. The hook with its words is now the song's chorus: answered in the in-seam, spoken in the tide, sung before the crest, sung by everyone at the crest, a last word at the out-seam. presence.py: the choir leads the crest at -5.6 dB against the mix, the whistle under it at -7.3. Also: the squeeze's second pass now has its company a THIRD below in D Mixolydian (harmony_key) instead of a fixed fourth; and the tide's chord gets a low fifth under it (A2 under D, G2 under C, F2 under B-flat) - compscore's one spectrum fault was a hole at 114 Hz (spectrum 82 -> 86, cohesion 92 -> 98). v15 95.59 (seeds 0/11 95.59/94.83, mean 95.21, vs v14 rescored now 95.14 on seed 0 and 95.17 on 11 - level on the mean; kept on judgment). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE 303 GOES. E2's cell has run the whole song on the acid patch - a resonant, driven squelch, the most aggressive sound in t6 and the kind of sound Harry's 'quite ugly chaos' was about. Now the same cell and the same notes play on a Berlin-school sequencer voice (moog-seq: a saw over a square sub through a resonant low-pass that snaps on each note, accents opening it), filtered under 3 kHz: an ostinato that murmurs under the hook (presence.py: -15.6 dB against the mix in the tide, the whistle at -3.7) instead of shouting over it. v16 95.91 (seeds 0/11 95.91/95.61 vs v15 rescored now 95.68 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: section, w8 (3:36-4:05, bars 113-128, the tear), flagged 'little new vs w7'. WHAT TO LISTEN FOR: at about 3:52, after the tape winds down and the one empty bar, the band snaps back - and now the chorus comes with it, home in D this time (at the crest it was lifted to E): the choir sings the line, 'the near side keeps the time / the far side lets it go', with a third above in D Mixolydian, twice, the voices alone carrying the tune (no whistle - the surge just had it), and on the second time the old voice sings with them. Then the out-seam, where he alone has the last word ('the far side lets it go'). A last chorus after the breakdown: the song's hook, with its words, as the storm's peak lets go. The tear's first half (kit playing E2 stretched, hats in 32nds, the stopped tape) is unchanged. Tried first with the whistle under the choir (94.64: too like the surge before it). Checked: w8 rewritten (residual -4 dB), w1-w7 untouched (-53 or below). Not heard by me.

v17 95.84 (seeds 0/11 95.84/95.59 vs v16 rescored now 95.91 on seed 0 and 95.61 on 11: level; kept on judgment). ROUND TYPE: section, w7 (3:06-3:36, bars 97-112, the surge), flagged static: the three-speed canon of E1 (cello twice as fast, whistle at its own speed, marimba twice as slow) ran unchanged for sixteen bars. WHAT TO LISTEN FOR: THE CANON CONVERGES - the surge keeps its canon for eight bars, then at about 3:23 the cello slows into step with the whistle (the same tune an octave and a half apart), and at about 3:29 the marimba speeds up to join them: for the surge's last four bars all three play E1 in unison across three octaves - the hook as plain and as big as it gets - and then the tear rips it apart (the stopped tape at 3:52). Polyphony gathering into one line, the storm's peak as agreement. v18 95.90 (seeds 0/11 95.90/95.74 vs v17 rescored now 95.86 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. LISTEN FOR the singers' leaps: every sung line in t6 - the old voice's answers, his line before the crest and his last word, his company a third below, and both choruses - now carries wM's singer's glide (glide_overshoot, pinned at 14:27, set subtle at 0.06): on each leap the pitch swings a little past the new note and settles, as a singer's does, instead of landing dead on it - most audible on the line's big leaps (D up to A, C down to G). The bold change I tried first and REFUSED in this round: an orchestration that breathes - each section leaving a colour out (the cello waiting for the tide, the pan stepping back in the tide, the marimba and hats silent in the squeeze, the sequencer and kora out of the cross); compscore's timbre spread barely moved (2.5 -> 2.8 dB) and recurrence collapsed (100 -> 42; a milder two-mute version 71) - t6's sections are heard as returns because they share their colours, so contrast here stays with the voices and the form. v19 95.70 (seeds 0/11 95.70/95.95, mean 95.83 vs v18 rescored now 95.90/95.74, mean 95.82: level; kept on judgment). v20 95.70 (seeds 0/11 95.70/96.05 vs v19 rescored now 95.70 on seed 0: level). ROUND TYPE: whole song. A FIX, IN HARRY'S DIRECTION (tone is home): since v14 put a low fifth at the bottom of every tide chord, the sequencer (E2's cell, from the pull to the surge, about three minutes) read that FIFTH as the chord's root - so over D it played A E C# G (a C#, out of D Mixolydian) and over C it played G D B F (an F a semitone against the chord's E). Counted over the whole track, the sequencer's notes were 99 C#s, 138 Fs and 165 Bs against 6 Cs and 15 F#s; now they are 224 Cs and 108 F#s, with the C#s, Fs and Bs gone outside the lifted crest. LISTEN FOR the sequencer under the pull, the tide and the cross (0:32-1:35, 2:36-3:06): the cell now sits inside the chords - D A F# C over D, C G E D over C - so the band's middle sounds consonant and settled where it used to rub, and the cell moves WITH the tide (D -> C) instead of a fifth away from it. The metric does not hear harmony (level); ears should. Not heard by me.

v21 95.71 (seeds 0/11 95.71/95.45 vs v20 rescored now 95.70 on seed 0, v20's 96.05 on seed 11: level / -0.6, recurrence 100 -> 96 on seed 11; kept on judgment). ROUND TYPE: whole song. LISTEN FOR (1) THE TIDE'S THIRD CHORD: for three minutes the tide rocked between two chords, D and C; now every fourth swing (the last two bars of each eight) it reaches G instead of C - G(add9) over its own D, the IV of D Mixolydian - so the phrase goes I - bVII, I - bVII, I - bVII, I - IV and has an end: the pull, the tide, the cross and the surge (0:32-1:35, 2:36-3:36) now sound like verses of a song rather than a loop. The sequencer follows it (G D B A on G) and the floor steps down to G1 under it (not in the in-seam, the squeeze or the out-seam's ebb). (2) THE SINGERS' SCOOP AND FALL (wM's play.scoop and play.fall, pinned at 17:07): the old voice and his lower part (scoop 1.5, fall 2.5 semitones) and both choruses (scoop 1, fall 2) now rise into the first note of each phrase from just below and let the last note sag as it dies - most audible on the old voice's last word, 'go', at the end, and on the chorus line ends. Not heard by me.

v22 96.62 (seeds 0/11 96.62/96.42 vs v21 rescored now 95.71: +0.9; variety 84 -> 93). ROUND TYPE: palette. THE FLOOR GETS A VOICE: the moving floor under the tide - D2 -> C2 -> G1, the chords' own roots, and since v21 the G of the new IV chord - was a second sine sub, felt rather than heard, on the album's most shared patch. Now it is an analog saw bass (Juno / SH-101: one saw through a dark low-pass, held for each chord's length), so the bass line you could only feel is a line you can hear: D, C, D, C, D, C, D, G under each eight bars. LISTEN FOR it under the pull and the tide (0:32-1:35) and especially at each turn to G. Also tried and refused this round: the crest's four lights on a Hammond B3 instead of the second harmonium (a gospel lift under the choir) - 94.43, recurrence 100 -> 91 and the seams worse. The cost here: the 61 Hz band is thinner (spectrum 90 -> 85) now that the sine left the floor. Not heard by me.

v23 96.75 (seeds 0/11 96.75/96.28 vs v22 rescored now 96.62 / v22's 96.42: level). ROUND TYPE: section, w2 (0:32-1:03, bars 17-32, the pull), flagged 'little new vs w1' and never worked: the kit and the sequencer arrived whole at bar 23, halfway through it.
